tb21_profile.skill: Read a Bayesian model in one language/library and reimplement it faithfully in another (RStan GP -> PyStan), preserving model structure, hyperparameters and RNG seed, then run posterior sampling and emit posterior means as numeric CSVs verified against ground truth
tb21_profile.domain: Bayesian statistics with Stan/PyStan, Gaussian-process regression (alpha/rho/sigma/beta, covariance kernels), MCMC/NUTS posterior sampling, and installing a pinned scientific package
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec / cross-language port: build an equivalent probabilistic script, sample, and write numeric parameter estimates checked for numerical agreement

notes: TMax is the only corpus with real MCMC/posterior-sampling content and it carries the task: task_005281, task_005102, task_002064, task_000032 all do posterior sampling with a fixed seed and write posterior means, exactly mirroring the alpha/sigma/rho/beta CSV deliverables and the seed=1 constraint. GP domain is thin everywhere; the strongest GP-structure matches are TMax's Cholesky/kernel tasks (task_000999, task_004494) and, outside TMax, gpflow-2096 and the sklearn GaussianProcessRegressor issue. Two distinct sub-skills split across corpora: (a) faithful posterior sampling with reproducibility -> TMax; (b) installing a pinned scientific package cleanly (PyStan 3.10.0) -> RTS conda/pyproject version-pin tasks and TW pyenv/conda installs. SWE-Smith is the weakest corpus here: it has essentially zero Bayesian/GP content (a 'Gaussian process|posterior|MCMC' search returned 2 near-irrelevant hits), so its list is filled with match-a-reference-implementation numeric bugs (dask lstsq/dtype, cloudpickle determinism) at overall<=3, chosen for the numeric-equivalence and determinism angle rather than domain. RTS also lacks any probabilistic-modelling task, so its list leans on version-pinned installs and statistical-summary scripts. No corpus contains an actual R-to-Python or Stan port; the cross-language-faithful-port skill is only weakly represented (py2->py3 ports exist in TMax but did not out-rank the MCMC matches). Merge note: several of these TMax MCMC tasks (task_005281, task_005102) also fit the raman-fitting/mcmc-style tasks - they are genuinely strong general Bayesian-inference training signal.
